transcript.content: Hi, I'm Dr. Smith. Welcome in—what brings you here today?
For the last few weeks, I’ve barely had any appetite. Even food I normally like after a shift, I just kind of stare at it and force down a few bites.
Over these past few weeks, have you also been feeling persistently sad, down, or empty most of the day?
Yeah. Most days I’ve got this heavy, flat feeling with me. Even when I’m at home with my family or sitting in the break room, I just feel like I’m not really there.
Besides the low mood, have you noticed that things you used to enjoy—hobbies, time with family, anything—just don't feel enjoyable or interesting to you anymore?
Yeah. I used to look forward to my morning runs, playing guitar, cooking dinner. Lately I just skip them—it all feels like chores I can’t really make myself care about.
Have you noticed any unintentional weight loss over these past few weeks?
I think so, yeah. I haven’t been eating much at all—just forcing down a few bites most of the time—so I’ve noticed my clothes feeling a little looser.
Have you ever had a period like this before—weeks of low mood, low energy, and loss of interest—prior to this current episode?
I’m not really sure. I can’t think of another time that was quite like this.
Besides the appetite and mood changes, have you noticed any night sweats, fevers, unusual lumps or swelling, or feeling unusually cold or hot compared to before?
No, I haven’t noticed any of those things.
Can you think of any specific stressful event or major change in your life—like a loss, job change, or relationship issue—that happened right before these feelings started?
Yeah. It started about three weeks ago, after the casino reorganized security and changed my assignments.
Have you been feeling unusually worthless, or blaming yourself excessively for things, during this time?
I don’t think so. I’ve been feeling down, but I’m not really blaming myself for things.
On your days off, when you're away from the casino and not thinking about the new assignment, does your mood and lack of interest still stay just as low, or do you notice some improvement?
It still stays pretty low. Even at home with my family, I feel this heavy, flat feeling most days—like I’m there, but not really present.

latest_inference.note: Mood and anhedonia remain persistently low even away from the workplace stressor (at home, days off), arguing against adjustment disorder and supporting a pervasive major depressive episode instead. Criteria for MDD (depressed mood, anhedonia, weight loss, >2 weeks duration, pervasive across contexts) are now well supported.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports approximately 3 weeks of persistent depressed/flat mood present nearly every day and pervasive across settings (home, work, family), marked anhedonia (loss of interest in running, guitar, cooking), decreased appetite with unintentional weight loss (clothes fitting looser). No prior similar episodes, no evidence of manic/hypomanic history, no worthlessness/guilt, no psychotic features, and symptoms not fully explained by a normal grief reaction or transient adjustment (mood persists independent of proximity to the stressor and pervades multiple domains of life). This clinical picture meets criteria for a major depressive episode; however, granular details on sleep, energy, concentration, psychomotor changes, and suicidality were not fully elicited, so severity/subtype specifiers cannot be assigned, supporting an 'unspecified' major depressive disorder code. Adjustment disorder was considered given the temporal link to a workplace stressor, but the persistence, breadth, and depth of vegetative/mood symptoms exceed typical adjustment reactions and better fit a full depressive syndrome.
